title: The Stories That Defined the Day
deck: Recovered FMB Daily Brief for 2026-08-18, reconstructed from FMB News' verified article archive. stories.headline: Senate Impeachment Court Cancels August 18 Session Amid Monsoon Flooding
stories.deck: The weather-related reset interrupts the trial calendar as flooding affects access to the Senate complex.
body: The approved FMB News overnight package reports that the Senate sitting as an Impeachment Court canceled the trial session scheduled for Tuesday, August 18, because severe monsoon rains and flooding disrupted Metro Manila travel.

The cancellation followed the Palace extension of alternative government work arrangements during the same weather emergency. The package attributes the trial-calendar decision to the Senate Impeachment Court and its presiding officer.
A weather-driven delay affects witness scheduling and the pace of a nationally consequential constitutional proceeding while reducing travel risk for court personnel, lawyers and witnesses.
Watch the Senate Impeachment Court for the next formal session notice, witness schedule and any further weather-related changes.

stories.headline: House Opens Scrutiny of Proposed ₱7.2-Trillion 2027 National Budget
stories.deck: The proposed spending plan is now under congressional review, with lawmakers examining how major allocations translate into public services and disaster resilience.
body: The FMB News overnight brief reports that the House of Representatives opened scrutiny of the proposed 2027 National Expenditure Program after its submission to Congress.

The National Expenditure Program is the executive branch's proposed spending plan. It is not yet the final General Appropriations Act and remains subject to congressional deliberation, amendment and approval.

The annual budget determines how public money is distributed across education, infrastructure, health, social protection, agriculture, security and other government functions. Scrutiny of implementation capacity matters because appropriations alone do not guarantee that projects will be completed on time or deliver their intended results.

Watch the House Committee on Appropriations for agency-by-agency hearings, proposed amendments and the timetable for moving the General Appropriations Bill to plenary debate. Also watch for official DBM budget tables that clarify final proposed allocations by department and program.

stories.headline: DBM Defends Proposed ₱976-Billion DepEd Budget and 6,587-Classroom Target
stories.deck: The education spending proposal is being tested against the country's classroom shortage and implementation capacity.
body: The approved FMB News package reports that budget officials defended a proposed ₱976-billion Department of Education allocation during House scrutiny of the 2027 National Expenditure Program.
The figures belong to the proposed 2027 spending plan and are not yet final enacted appropriations. Congress can amend agency allocations before passage of the General Appropriations Act.
Classroom shortages affect class size, learning conditions and access. The effectiveness of a large appropriation depends on procurement, site readiness, construction capacity and project delivery.
Watch House budget hearings, DBM tables and DepEd implementation plans for changes to the proposed amount, classroom count and delivery model.

stories.headline: Classes and Government Work Suspended in NCR and 14 Provinces for August 18
stories.deck: The emergency measures expand across Luzon as heavy monsoon rain continues to create flood and travel risks.
body: The approved FMB News overnight package reports that in-person classes and standard government on-site work were suspended across Metro Manila and 14 provinces for Tuesday, August 18.
The suspension package was issued during an extended period of enhanced Southwest Monsoon rainfall. Essential and frontline services remain subject to separate operational requirements.
School and work suspension orders directly affect commuting, public-service access and household safety decisions during severe weather.
Residents should follow the latest Palace, LGU, school and agency notices because coverage and resumption arrangements can change by locality and function.

stories.headline: Zamboanga School Shooting Probe Traces Firearm to Bureau of Customs Issue
stories.deck: The firearm finding shifts attention to weapon custody and how a minor gained access to a government-issued gun.
body: The approved FMB News evening package reports that police and interior officials traced a firearm used in the Ateneo de Zamboanga shooting to a government-issued sidearm associated with the Bureau of Customs.
The shooting left the student victim and suspected student shooter dead and triggered scrutiny of school safety, firearm storage and child protection.
The provenance of the weapon raises questions about government firearm accountability and household safekeeping without establishing criminal liability by any particular person.
Watch the PNP, DILG and Bureau of Customs for chain-of-custody findings, administrative action and any policy changes on firearm storage.

stories.headline: OCD Brief Reports 26 Fatalities and 5.1 Million Affected as Red Rain Alerts Hit Luzon
stories.deck: The cumulative disaster picture worsened as evacuation, rainfall and reservoir concerns remained active.
body: The approved FMB News midday package, citing the Office of Civil Defense and NDRRMC, reports 26 disaster fatalities and 5,114,300 affected individuals across 10 regions as of midday August 18.
These are cumulative disaster-response figures reported by the approved newsroom package. Affected population, displaced population and fatalities are different measures and should not be combined.
The figures help show the scale of the emergency and the pressure on evacuation, relief and local response systems.
Watch OCD and NDRRMC situation reports for validation of casualties, missing persons, displacement, damage and assistance totals.
